The first customer was Marta, who wanted to check a birthday order she had placed the previous week. She said the cake was for her father, and the pickup was planned for Saturday after the family concert.

Jules found that note in the comment box and copied it onto the fresh form. She also confirmed that the cake should serve twelve and that the delivery was not included because Marta would collect it herself.

The new sheet has a box for the person collecting the order and another box for the person receiving the invoice. Jules explained the difference because customers had sometimes put a guest name in the wrong place. “Please put Quentin, not Mina, in the pickup name box,” Marta said. Quentin was her brother, and he would arrive after work, while Mina, her cousin, had offered to pay the deposit online. Section one is the cake information, and section two is the collection information. Jules read each line aloud while Marta followed on her phone. Section one showed orange sponge, almond cream, raspberry preserve, serves twelve, and no message on top. The allergy box said almonds, and the note said the cake would be kept away from the walnut display. Marta asked whether the almond cream was made in the same room as the walnut pastries. Jules said the mixing bench was shared but cleaned before each recipe, and she did not promise an entirely separate preparation area. Marta said that was useful to know and kept the order as written.

The form also asked whether a candle set was needed. Marta said no candles because her father would bring his own from home. She asked for a sturdy cake board and a tall carton, since the cake had a narrow sugar decoration that could catch on a shallow lid. Jules checked the supply shelf and marked one tall carton on the order. The display sample used a wide board, but the bakery had a smaller round board that fit the cake without extending beyond the carton base. Marta said to use that one and asked Jules to note that the decoration should face forward when the box was opened.

While they were checking the collection time, the oven alarm sounded in the back room, and the baker called that the morning batch of sourdough was ready. Jules stepped away to turn off the timer and returned with flour on one sleeve. She apologized and asked Marta to repeat the time. Marta said Saturday at three thirty in the afternoon, not three in the morning. Jules wrote three thirty pm beside the date and read the whole line back. Marta confirmed it and said Quentin usually came from the west side, so the later slot gave him enough time after his shift.

Tessa, the shift lead, came over to approve the change from the damaged copy and looked at the note about the collection name. Tessa said, “The blue pencil is for changes that still need a customer check, and the black pen is for details the customer has confirmed.” Jules had used blue for the first version of the pickup name, so she crossed that entry with a single line and wrote Quentin in black. Marta watched the correction and said Mina should remain on the contact record because she might call with a question about the deposit, but she should not be listed as the collector.

Before Marta left, Jules clipped the receipt behind the new form and checked that the total matched the online payment record. The deposit was twenty dollars, and the remaining balance was due at collection. The receipt included a small charge for the tall carton and showed no delivery fee. Jules told Marta the bakery could not guarantee that the raspberry layer would look identical to the photograph because the fruit was prepared in small batches. Marta said she understood and asked that the outside remain plain with no colored piping. The cake would be finished on Friday after the afternoon cooling period.

Marta took a photo of the confirmed order details and saved it with the bakery phone number in her contacts. She also asked Jules to call if the pickup time changed because Quentin was arranging a ride with a coworker and needed to know before Saturday. Jules wrote Marta as the person to call and recorded her mobile number on the reverse of the form. The bakery kept the original in the Saturday tray and gave Marta a copy with the collection date circled in pencil. The new paper was dry, and the corrected names were easy to read."}]
